concerns.text: T019 Step 1 requires manual 'Verify the DOI resolves... and identify the direct download link' before fetching. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which mandates 'External datasets MUST be fetched from the same canonical source on every run' via automation. A manual step breaks the 'fresh GitHub Actions runner' reproducibility guarantee.

T022b Step 5 instructs to 'assign the **first [deferred] of the validation set (by index)** to the SC-003 Validation set'. The use of '[deferred]' here leaves the sample size undefined. SC-003 requires measuring if substructures are present in '>80% of high-yield reactions'. Without a defined sample size or selection logic (e.g., 'first 100' or 'top 10%'), the task cannot satisfy the acceptance criterion, effectively weakening the requirement.

T024 and T025 contain placeholders '[deferred]' for chunk sizes and retry thresholds in 'Memory Enforcement' logic. FR-009 mandates 'runs within ≤ 7.0 GB RAM'. Leaving these critical parameters undefined renders the task non-executable and the success criterion untestable, violating the requirement for deterministic execution.

T033b relies on a 'generic reaction template' or 'heuristic bond analysis' without specifying exact chemical logic or RDKit parameters. FR-008 requires mapping bits to reaction centers. Ambiguity in the algorithm prevents deterministic verification and risks non-reproducible results, violating Constitution Principle I and FR-008.

T035a Step 1 defines 'high-yield' as 'top quantile... (i.e., yield > np.percentile(yields, 90))'. However, SC-003 requires the top 3 substructures to be present in '>80% of high-yield reactions'. The task does not explicitly link the '90th percentile' definition to the 'high-yield' term used in SC-003 verification, creating a semantic gap where the success criterion's definition of 'high-yield' is not strictly preserved in the task logic.
